meta.title: RideFlux — live dashboard for electric unicycles
meta.description: RideFlux shows your electric unicycle's speed, battery, temperature and PWM load live on your phone, warns you before a limit, records every trip, and can drive a heads-up display on AR glasses. No ads, no tracking, open source.
nav.label: Main
hero.eyebrow: Open source · No ads · No data collected
hero.title: Your wheel, live — on your phone and in your line of sight.
hero.lead: RideFlux connects to your electric unicycle over Bluetooth and shows speed, battery, temperature and PWM load while you ride. It warns you before a limit, records every trip, and can drive a heads-up display on AR glasses.
features.title: Everything you need on the ride
f.dash.d: Speed gauge, battery, voltage, current, power and temperatures at a glance — plus BMS details, live charts, and parameter and event pages.
f.alerts.d: Warnings for overspeed, over-temperature, low battery and high PWM load. You set the thresholds, and a value hovering on a limit won't spam you.
f.trips.d: A ride starts recording when the wheel starts moving. Every trip keeps its route, speed, voltage and current.
f.export.d: Export any trip as CSV or GPX for other tools, or back up all trips and settings to a single ZIP file.
f.controls.d: Headlight, horn, speed limit, calibration and more — where your wheel supports them, and locked while you are moving.
f.hud.d: Send speed and battery to Rokid AR glasses so you can keep your eyes up. A Bluetooth ring shows or hides it.

hud.title: Keep your eyes up
hud.lead: Pair RideFlux with Rokid AR glasses and the essentials sit in your line of sight — no more glancing down at a phone on the handlebar.
hud.b1: **One link to the wheel.** The phone holds the wheel's single Bluetooth connection and relays a compact frame to the glasses, so two devices never fight over it. The glasses can also read the wheel directly.
hud.b2: **Only your phone.** The glasses pair to a token your phone creates, and the phone streams only to glasses you approved.
hud.b3: **Hands-free.** A Bluetooth ring shows or hides the HUD. A safety alert still breaks through when it is hidden.
hud.b4: **Optional.** The phone app is a complete dashboard on its own.
hud.get.d: The HUD app for Rokid glasses is an APK on GitHub Releases, for sideloading.
wheels.title: Supported wheels
wheels.lead: RideFlux speaks the protocols of the main electric unicycle brands. Here is what has actually been tested on a real wheel.
wheels.begode.note: Verified on a Begode A2. A few readings (trip distance, PWM) are known to be off and are being fixed.
wheels.legend.verified: **Verified on hardware** — the developer connected a real wheel of that model and checked the app against it.
wheels.legend.exp: **Experimental** — implemented from open-source references and recorded test frames, but not yet tried on a real wheel. It may misread values on yours, so compare it with your wheel's own display before relying on it for safety.
wheels.cta.t: Own a wheel marked experimental? A short test report helps a lot.
wheels.disclaimer: RideFlux is an independently developed third-party app and is not affiliated with any wheel manufacturer or Rokid. Brand names belong to their owners.
privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.lead: RideFlux does not collect, transmit, sell or share personal data.
privacy.p1: **No internet permission.** The app cannot send anything off your phone.
privacy.p2: **No ads, analytics, crash reporting or accounts.**
privacy.p3: **Location only while recording.** It draws a trip's route, and is never requested in the background.
privacy.p4: **Your data stays yours.** Trips stay on your phone until you export them, and Android cloud backup is off.
faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.q1: Which wheels does it work with?
faq.a1: Begode/Gotway, KingSong, Veteran, Ninebot and Inmotion are implemented. So far only the Begode A2 has been verified on a real wheel; the rest are experimental — see the table above.
faq.a2: No. The glasses HUD is optional, and the phone app is a complete dashboard on its own.
faq.a3: No. There is no internet permission, no ads, no analytics and no accounts. Trips are stored on your phone and leave it only if you export them.
faq.q4: Why does it ask for Bluetooth, location and notification permissions?
faq.a4: Bluetooth connects to your wheel, glasses and ring. Location draws a trip's route while recording; on Android 11 and older it is also required to scan for Bluetooth devices. Notifications carry alerts and the recording indicator.
faq.q6: Can I change settings while riding?
faq.a6: Speed limit, calibration, power off and other wheel controls are locked while the wheel is moving. Please keep your eyes on the road and do not operate your phone while riding.
faq.q7: A reading looks wrong. What should I do?
faq.a7: Compare it with your wheel's own display, then [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/zero2005x/RideFlux/issues) with your wheel's model and firmware. Reports on experimental wheels help the most.
